title: LEGO Ideas' La Catrina: fan designer shares his reaction to the finished set
summary: The designer behind the upcoming 21372 La Catrina LEGO Ideas set has spoken about seeing his Day of the Dead-inspired submission become an official product.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
José Miguel Medina Pérez (known online as yop1172), the fan designer behind the 10K LEGO Ideas submission that inspired 21372 La Catrina, has discussed the set's journey from concept to shelf in a LEGO Ideas blog post covered by Brick Fanatics. The 1,212-piece posable figure celebrates Día de los Muertos, the Mexican Day of the Dead, and was inspired by a trip José took to Capula in Michoacán, Mexico, where he saw clay Catrina sculptures.

José explained how he moved from an anatomically-focused skeleton design to building the elaborate dress, eventually using small ball-joint pieces rather than SNOT techniques to achieve fabric-like folds. The finished official set includes brick-built marigolds and monarch butterflies, plus printed sugar skull decorations on the hat and dress.

Despite some size reduction and changes from his original design, José has given his approval to the final LEGO Ideas product, saying the team did a great job retaining the elements that made his model special.

## Why it matters
This is a nice look behind the scenes at how a LEGO Ideas submission gets reworked for mass production, and it's useful for fans who want to understand the design compromises involved. It also highlights another culturally-themed set joining the LEGO Ideas line-up, which will interest collectors and those who enjoy display-focused builds.

## What to watch next
21372 La Catrina is due to arrive next month, so expect official pricing, piece count confirmation and wider reviews once it's fully available.

title: LEGO Ideas reveals why 21372 La Catrina ended up smaller than the original fan design
summary: LEGO designers have explained how the skull detailing and arm posing shaped the final scale of the upcoming 21372 La Catrina set, based on comments made at a fan media roundtable.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
LEGO Ideas has shared new details about 21372 La Catrina, a 1,212-piece set based on a winning fan submission by yop1172 (José Miguel Medina Pérez). According to comments made by the LEGO Ideas design team at a roundtable with fan media, reported by Brick Fanatics, the finished model ended up noticeably smaller than the original fan design.

Designer Jim Clayton said he used other LEGO buildable figures as a starting point for sizing, before focusing heavily on the skull, which he described as the trickiest part to get right. He reportedly built more than 100 test versions of the skull, which is constructed partly upside down and then sandwiched together, before settling on a final approach that balanced detail, strength and buildability.

LEGO Ideas design manager Jordan David Scott also pointed to the figure's arms as a key factor. The original fan design relied on a support structure to hold certain poses, whereas the official LEGO set apparently took a different approach, which further influenced the overall scale of the finished model.

## Why it matters
This gives fans a behind-the-scenes look at how LEGO Ideas designers balance faithfulness to a fan's original concept with the practical demands of buildability, stability and detail. For collectors watching 21372 La Catrina, it also helps explain the size and design choices ahead of the set's full release.

## What to watch next

title: LEGO Ideas submission based on Supernatural disappears from review without explanation
summary: A fan-made LEGO Ideas project inspired by the TV show Supernatural has quietly vanished from the second 2026 review round, with no official reason given so far.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
A LEGO Ideas submission called Dean's Baby Supernatural (TV SHOW), created by fan designer SamSamSamy, has disappeared from the line-up of the second LEGO Ideas review of 2026. The project had only recently passed the crucial 10,000 supporter mark, qualifying it for review consideration.

The build recreated the iconic car from the Supernatural TV series, using around 450 pieces. It featured a removable roof, seating inside, an engine detail under the bonnet, weapons stored in the boot, and minifigures of the show's main characters, Dean, Sam and Castiel.

As of now, there's been **no official explanation** from LEGO for the removal. This has happened before — in 2023, projects including a Gothic Castle build and one based on The Neverending Story were also pulled from review, with the latter reportedly withdrawn following a copyright complaint from the licence holder. Given Supernatural is a licensed TV property, a similar rights issue is a plausible explanation here, but this is currently **speculation only** and unconfirmed by LEGO or LEGO Ideas.

With the project gone, the second 2026 review now sits at 47 qualifying fan-designed submissions, with results not expected until next year.

## Why it matters
LEGO Ideas is one of the few official routes for fan designs to become real sets, so any submission being pulled — especially after it's already cleared the tough 10K threshold — is notable for builders and fans following the community pipeline. It's also a useful reminder that licensed or copyrighted content can pose extra risk for creators hoping to see their designs made official.

## What to watch next
Fans will be watching for any official statement from LEGO Ideas clarifying the removal, as well as the eventual results of this review round, expected in 2027.

Among the projects said to have made it through are concepts based on Jumanji, Universal Monsters, an iMac, and Naruto's Ichiraku Ramen Shop, alongside a handful of other fan favourites. Meanwhile, dozens of creative pitches — covering everything from a Converse Chuck Taylor build to a BBC Ghosts set and a Twilight Zone Tower of Terror model — didn't make the cut this time.

The good news for rejected creators is that they're free to resubmit their projects and try to reach 10,000 supporters again to qualify for a future review.

## Why it matters
LEGO Ideas is one of the few official routes for fan concepts to become real sets, so review results are always closely watched by the community. title: LEGO SpongeBob SquarePants Returns After 14 Years
summary: LEGO has officially revealed two new SpongeBob SquarePants sets, ending a 14-year gap since the theme last appeared on shelves.

LEGO has officially unveiled two new SpongeBob SquarePants sets: LEGO Icons 11386 SpongeBob SquarePants: Bikini Bottom and 40858 SpongeBob SquarePants Figure. Early releases like 3825 Krusty Krab and 3826 Build-A-Bob introduced Bikini Bottom to builders, while later sets such as 4981 The Chum Bucket and 3831 Rocket Ride expanded the cast with characters like Sandy Cheeks. In 2009, LEGO revisited its earliest designs with updated versions of the Krusty Krab and pineapple house, before the theme wound down by 2012 as LEGO shifted focus to other properties like Atlantis and Hero Factory.

## Why it matters
For UK collectors and fans of nostalgic licensed themes, this is a significant official comeback. Twenty-two years after SpongeBob SquarePants first aired, and 14 years after LEGO last touched Bikini Bottom, this return could open the door to further sets if demand is strong — something display builders and IP collectors will want to watch closely.

Space-themed LEGO sets have a strong following among collectors and display builders, and a dedicated Hubble model has been a long time coming given the telescope's cultural and scientific significance.
